# Introduction

This is the introduction. Every section that needs a number is
labelled and referenced, never described as "the section above".
For example, the security commitments are in @sec-commitments and the
data summary is in @tbl-data.

## Purpose

The format produces a clean, professional PDF for print and offline
use, and an HTML version for reading. Both come from this single
source. The PDF carries its baseline so a recipient's copy is
traceable to the repository state it was built from.

## Scope

The format is for business documents: policies, proposals, reports,
and anything distributed in confidence. It follows the document
standards in the standards library, adapted to a neutral
professional style. The configuration-management and writing
standards that govern the underlying processes are [@jsp945; @jsp101],
and the security posture follows [@iso27001] and the Cyber
Governance Code [@cybergovernance]. Writing is controlled language
per ASD-STE100 [@ste100].

# Security commitments {#sec-commitments}

The business commits to:

- Two-factor authentication on every account
- Signed commits on all repositories
- No secrets in repositories
- Dependency and vulnerability scanning
- Incident response with a written process

A missed commitment is recorded in the risk register, not hidden.
This is a callout demonstration:

::: {.callout-warning}
Confidential documents carry the marking set in the front matter.
Do not forward them without the owner's consent.
:::

# Data summary

@fig-logo shows the brand mark. Figures use numbered captions and
appear in the List of Figures, the same way tables appear in the
List of Tables.

![Obsidian Solutions brand mark](obsidian-logo.png){#fig-logo fig-alt="The Obsidian Solutions brand mark, a dark geometric glyph on white."}

@tbl-data summarises what the backup policy covers. The inventory
lists every data class the policy protects, the system that holds it,
and whether the nightly backup covers it. Secrets are not backed up
in plaintext; the secrets manager export path is the recovery route.

| Data | Source | Covered |
|---|---|---|
| Repositories | GitHub organisation | Yes, nightly mirror |
| Policy and documentation | business-policy | Yes |
| Client notes and configurations | working files | Yes |
| Secrets | secrets manager | Export path |

: Data coverage summary {#tbl-data}

# Conclusion

This example is a template, not a policy. Copy it, replace the front
matter and content, and render with the `render.sh` script. The
resulting PDF and HTML ship together: PDF for print, HTML for
reading.^[Footnotes demonstrate the footnote style.]

# Compliance matrix {.appendix}

The compliance matrix maps each control in this document to the
governing standard. It demonstrates the appendix feature: sections
after an `{.appendix}` heading are numbered A, B, C and listed in
the table of contents.

| Control | Standard |
|---|---|
| Two-factor authentication | @cybergovernance |
| Configuration management | @jsp945 |
| Document control | @jsp101 |

# Glossary {.appendix}

A short glossary demonstrates a second appendix section. The letter
comes from LaTeX's `\appendix` switch, so the heading has no letter
of its own.

- **Baseline**: the repository state a document was built from.
- **Classification**: the confidentiality marking carried in the
  running header and PDF metadata.
